subject: AI & Agents
title: Recognizing Faces
description: A short lesson to help you apply Recognizing Faces.

hook.text: Your phone unlocks by scanning your face in 0.3 seconds. How does it know it's you?

buildup.text: Facial recognition maps key points — distance between eyes, jawline shape, nose width.

discovery.text: It converts your face into a unique numerical fingerprint and compares it against stored ones.

twist.text: Identical twins can fool some systems, and lighting changes trip up cheaper models.

climax.text: China uses it for payments. The EU debates banning it in public spaces.

punchline.text: Your face is a password you can never change.

quiz.question: How does facial recognition identify a person?
options: Maps facial features into a numerical fingerprint

details.summary: Facial recognition AI maps faces into mathematical representations called embeddings, comparing distances between them to identify individuals. The technology is powerful but raises serious privacy and bias concerns.
details.whyItMatters: Facial recognition is used for phone unlocking, security, and surveillance. Its accuracy varies across demographics, making bias and privacy critical issues that affect millions of people.
takeaways: Face recognition converts faces into numerical embeddings
It compares embedding distances to identify or verify people
Accuracy varies across demographics, raising bias concerns

faq.question: How accurate is facial recognition AI?
faq.answer: Top systems exceed 99% accuracy on benchmark tests. However, accuracy drops significantly for darker skin tones, women, and faces with unusual angles or lighting, creating concerning disparities.

faq.question: Why is facial recognition controversial?
faq.answer: It enables mass surveillance without consent. Accuracy disparities mean marginalized groups face higher misidentification rates. Several cities have banned government use of facial recognition over these concerns.
